hook_b: Bengaluru to Hyderabad in *2 hours*: Vaishnaw names the South Bullet Train route
tldr: Railway Minister Vaishnaw says the proposed South Bullet Train will link Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Amaravati and Chennai.

beats.what: On Nov 1, Ashwini Vaishnaw announced the South Bullet Train corridor's cities.
beats.why: Vaishnaw spoke in Bengaluru; the report summary gives no cost or timeline.
beats.care: A Hyderabad–Bengaluru trip could take about 2 hours, if the proposed line is built.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said in Bengaluru on Sunday, November 1 that the proposed South Bullet Train corridor would connect Bengaluru with Hyderabad, Amaravati and Chennai (Siasat). Siasat's headline puts Bengaluru–Hyderabad at 2 hours. He also said a Vande Bharat service between Bengaluru and Mangaluru will start in the coming weeks, once electrification and testing are done. Cost, route alignment and a timeline for the bullet corridor were not in the report summary we read.

cards.q: Hyderabad–Bengaluru bullet train: what's your condition?
Which city is NOT on the proposed South Bullet Train corridor?
cards.why: Vaishnaw named Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Amaravati and Chennai.

viz.l: Cities on the proposed South corridor

insight: The South corridor would also connect Amaravati and Chennai, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said.

learn.t: A corridor is the planned route; it still needs surveys, approval and funding before work starts.

watch: A detailed project report, cost and alignment for the South corridor.
